planned_arguments.prompt:
Edit this inspected poster into its assigned coherent flat graphic construction. ONE complete opaque 16:9 landscape poster. The observed problem is that the useful facts are all confined inside the large rectangular screen, the four practical entries become small at 720x405, and detailed scenic rendering overwhelms the hard-edge apparatus/light/bridge relationship.

Repair the spatial construction: let one continuous, sharply bounded chartreuse widening optical plane run from the large cropped projector's lens at lower-left across the right two-thirds BEFORE it reaches a distinct supported cinema screen at the far-right edge. The projector aims at the screen. Move the time/date/venue and practical information into the broad clear part of that beam, with the supported screen visibly beyond the information. Keep a generous optical boundary around the information, rather than a thick panel, screen rectangle, sidebar, ruled table or footer. Screen may be partly cropped at the right but must still read as a supported landscape cinema screen, with visible coherent frame and stand. Bridge deck/underside remains a substantive coral flat construction near the outer upper crop. Use the beam, apparatus and screen as connected functional graphic shapes.

Simplify the projector, bridge, riverbank and adults into clean hard-edged flat planes and strong silhouettes with a few purposeful internal shapes. Remove elaborate building windows, glowing street lamps, water reflections, photorealistic anatomy/clothing, volumetric shading and dense scenic detail. Retain only controlled local halftone in structural shadows/projector body. No gradients over letterforms. A grounded seated group of adult viewers on mats and one adult standing speaker at the far right must remain clearly legible. The speaker's hand and forearm own the microphone held near the mouth; the other hand can gesture separately. Preserve recognizable outdoor film screening and conversation, approachable adult cultural tone, dark plum/chartreuse/coral palette, pale title, title-leading-to-time hierarchy and broad light grouping.

Typography correction: keep the compact heavy square two-line left headline, its English and descriptor above the projector and outside the beam. The time is the bright plane's largest useful fact; date and venue follow directly. All four practical entries need visibly larger semibold type and generous spacing: around 34–36 px on a 1280x720 DESIGN plane, so about 19–20 px at the actual 720x405 usage view. Make room by reducing scenic detail, projector/frame size or title area as necessary. These are design proportions, not an output pixel size. Do not squeeze into the taper. Reserve a broad approximately 600+ design-pixel span for practical information, with entry/capacity followed by preparation/weather. Protect all letters from beam boundaries, silhouettes and structural overlaps.

Every existing required entry must remain verbatim, exactly once, with no new print. Complete protected copy:
"다리 아래 영화관"
"BRIDGE CINEMA"
"야외 단편 상영 · 감독과의 대화"
"2026.12.05 토요일"
"18:00–20:30"
"홍제천 연가교 아래"
"17:30부터 입장"
"돗자리 지참"
"무료 관람 · 선착순 80명"
"우천 시 실내로 변경"
Only soft breaks at existing word boundaries. Keep square Hangul proportions, open counters, complete strokes, clear word spaces and crisp Korean/English. Preserve visibly distinct two-dot colons, horizontal range dash and exact middle-dot glyph class with optical gaps. Do not add titles, captions, logos, watermark, QR, labels, credits, pseudo-print, tiny filler text, physical tape, contact sheet or mockup. One separate flat landscape poster with no border. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력

observed_repair_cause: Facts are entirely on screen rather than broad beam.
Four practical entries have roughly 11–12 px glyph height at usage720.
Detailed scenery and volumetric drawing displace assigned flat graphic planes.
maintained_features: All ten copy entries and their punctuation.
Left title to right time reading path.
Connected projector/light/screen under bridge with grounded adult viewers and mic-holding speaker.
